messages:
maria: Heads-up: started seeing sustained queue growth on us-west-gpu-pool at 10:14 UTC, tail p95 gen latency hitting 1.2s for large-context models. Queues ~220 while capacity shows 85% GPU utilization.
ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-pool-us-west: queue_depth>200 for 3m, latency_p95>1s.
kai: Is this traffic spike customer-driven or background batch? any tenant skew?
maria: Mostly live requests from a handful of clients (chat + codegen). Not batch. Looks like two big tenants pushing concurrent sessions after a release.
tom: If we cross-region route to eu-west, SLA-sensitive customers will see +80–120ms RTT. Need to consider SLA tiers before just spilling.
sam: We should consider model fallback (4k -> 2k quantized) for non-enterprise routes first. That cuts GPU time ~40% in our bench. But quality drop for codegen clients could be obvious.
carol: Can we do partial routing: 25% traffic to fallback model, 15% to eu-west, rest stay with admission control? That gives graceful degradation vs. wholesale spill.
kai: I like a three-lever approach: 1) SLA-aware admission (reject/queue/shape by tier), 2) local model fallback for tolerant routes, 3) cross-region spill only for best-effort traffic.
maria: Agreed. Proposed immediate policy (concept):
```yaml
admission_policy:
  priority_classes:
    - name: enterprise
      action_on_saturation: queue
      max_concurrency_per_tenant: 20
    - name: standard
      action_on_saturation: shed_percent
      shed_percent: 20
    - name: best_effort
      action_on_saturation: route_cross_region
      route_percent: 30
fallback_rules:
  model_tier_map:
    - from: gptx-large
      to: gptx-medium-quant
      when: gpu_util>80% and queue_depth>100
    - from: embed-v2
      to: embed-v2-quant
      when: gpu_util>85%
```

sam: That looks fine as a starting point. Important to include per-tenant token-rate budgets, otherwise one noisy tenant will still blow concurrency slots.
carol: Also need a short-circuit: if cross-region RTT + processing pushes total latency > customer_sla, then prefer shedding/fallback even for best-effort.
tom: Cost note: cross-region spill adds egress $$$ and may trigger inter-region quota limits for some clients. Add cost_threshold gating to route_cross_region.
kai: For simulation, I ran a quick calc: if 30% of best-effort goes to eu-west, eu-west GPU ops increase ~12% for our current traffic — shouldn't overflow eu-west unless there are simultaneous spikes. But network egress ~0.6TB/hr at peak -> incremental $/hr ~ moderate.
maria: Can ops-runtime implement a route-sculpting operator that takes these inputs: per-pool gpu_util, queue_depth, tenant_tier, token_rate, and outputs per-request decision (serve_local / fallback / route_cross_region / reject)?
aiops: (auto) ingest metrics: gpu_util, queue_depth, active_sessions, per_tenant_concurrency.
carol: We'll need canary rollout: 1) run policy in dry-run for 30m with sampled traffic, 2) run 5% live traffic with fallback+routing, monitor user-facing latency and quality regressions for codegen tenants.
sam: Add telemetry hooks: tag requests with decision_reason and model_version so we can correlate quality regressions with fallback.
maria: Action items:
- maria: open infra ticket to add tenant token budgets and admission gating (ETA 3d)
- kai: prepare simulator run for policy scenarios and post numbers (ETA today EOD)
- sam: add telemetry flags for decision_reason and model_version in runtime (ETA 2d)
- tom: prepare cost gating thresholds and egress budget config (ETA 1d)
- carol: plan canary steps and target tenants (ETA tomorrow)

kai: Quick numbers from sim (WIP): with current load, enforcement of max_concurrency_per_tenant=20 drops queue_depth from 220->90 and p95 latency from 1.2s->0.6s. Fallback on 30% of standard reduces GPU time by ~28%.
maria: Nice. Let's start dry-run in us-west with decision logs on for 30 minutes. If stable, roll to 5% live routing.
carol: I'll coordinate with solutions-eng to notify affected enterprise customers about possible model fallback during the canary window.
maria: Thanks all. Setting up dry-run job now and will post instrumentation logs in this thread. :thumbsup:
